rules_text:
Rules summary Dice Values In a Rob attempt: • White die in Submissive (and Passive) Parishes and Nottingham: die faces are -2 -1 -1 0 1 2 • Green die in Revolting Parishes and Forests: die faces are -1 -1 0 1 2 3 Royal Inspection Procedure Unrest Phase One Carriage is moved if possible. Shift Royal Favour as follows: Submissive Parishes Outcome 5 - 7 1 step towards Order 3 - 4 1 step towards Justice 1 - 2 2 steps towards Justice 0 3 steps towards Justice Check for Game End • First two Royal Inspections: 5 + Justice or Order immediately ends game. • Last Royal Inspection: Final position determines winner. Mischief Robin Hood: • Gains 1 Shilling for each Camp in a Forest (including Ollerton Hill) • May conduct a single Rob Plot followed by a Donate Deed in up to two spaces. • Returns half (rounded down) of the Merry Men in Prison to Available Forces (can include Robin Hood if imprisoned). Governance Sheriff: • Gains 1 Shilling for each Submissive space (including Nottingham). • Removes half (rounded down) of the Henchmen in each Revolting space to Available Forces. • Sets any Revolting Parish where Henchmen still outnumber Merry Men to Submissive. Redeployment Sheriff: • Must move any Henchmen in Revolting Parishes and Forests to Submissive spaces. • May move any other Henchmen to Nottingham. • Returns all Used Carriages to Available Forces. Robin Hood: • Merry Men on the map are flipped to Hidden. • Merry Men in Submissive Parishes must be moved to any Forest, or to a Parish with a Camp (even if Submissive). • Any other Merry Men may either stay where they are or may be moved to a Forest or a Parish with a Camp. • If Robin Hood piece is in Available Forces, place it in any Forest. • Unless Robin Hood is in Prison, player may secretly swap the Robin Hood piece with any other Merry Man on the map. Robin Hood always starts new Ballad as First Eligible Player.

[Rating: 1/10] A real disappointment to see that the game does not bring new things to the table compared to other games of this style such as TBW. I prefer this last mentioned game, with an original and historical theme, than another one based on practically a children's story (I already have the Disney movie for this theme). I think that an author who calls himself this way should work more on innovating and not just copying.

[Rating: 2/10] BGA game - Really didn't enjoy this one, it might be my own understanding that was poor. Which is a shame as I do like the Robin Hood theme!

[Rating: 3/10] So I had a very small COIN-journey: Played Cubra Libre, British Way, Andean Abyss, Vija and this one. I am probably not the right person to play this genre, as I am getting headache in planning my actions ahead. Cuba Libra was a burden for me, as Andean Abyss was also: The cards feel way too strong and having to pass each second turn is for me torture. I know that others love these mechanics, and I do understand the strategic layers that are implemented – it is just not for me.   This being said, A Gest of Robin Hood is definitely the best entry game in the COIN series (although some would say

[Rating: 3/10] It does what it says on the tin -  a quick simplified COIN game for two players only, The only alternative was Colonial Twilight which is much more complex and longer. But unfortunately, I don't seem to enjoy the COIN system in the end, i will just keep Falling Sky and go back to CDG's. So low rating due to personal preferences, not the quality of the design

[Rating: 3/10] A couple early mistakes can easily lead you to positions in which you have no agency or ability to impact the game. The only saving grace is that there's a mercy rule to end the game early. Yikes, I had high hopes for this but it was rough.

[Rating: 3/10] A 2 player asymmetric action selection game of trickery where players are building up units and trying to influence locations, gaining resources, and claim locations for victory. This didn't hit the spot for me.

[Rating: 4/10] Love the art, setting, thematic integration of system and topic, the production values are top notch. However, the results felt too incremental, procedural, and tit-for-tat for me.

[Rating: 4/10] Bastante decepcionante. Un poco farragoso para lo que en realidad es. En un primer acercamiento me llevé una gran decepción porque mis expectativas eran tal vez demasiado altas. Se queda un poco a medias de todo. Con el sistema tampoco es que me haya volado la cabeza.
